framework.name: Strategic Priority 1 - Sustainable and inclusive economic growth, industrial, rural and agricultural development, food security and nutrition

children.name: Outcome 1.1 - By 2022, inclusive and sustainable industrial, agricultural and rural development contribute to economic growth, decent work, improved livelihoods, food security and nutrition, especially among women and vulnerable groups

framework.name: Strategic Priority 2 - Good Governance, rule of law, human rights, gender equality

children.name: Outcome 2.1 - By 2022, institutions at all levels are more accountable and inclusive ensuring justice, human rights, gender equality and sustainable peace for all

framework.name: Strategic Priority 3 - Environment, climate change, and disaster risk management

children.name: Outcome 3.1 - By 2022, communities are more resilient to climate and disaster risks and are engaged in sustainable and inclusive natural resource management and risk-informed development

framework.name: Strategic Priority 4 - Social sector development (social and child protection, health and education)

children.name: Outcome 4.1 - By 2022, social protection, health and education systems are more effective and inclusive, and provide quality services

framework.name: Output 4.1.7 - Population has increased ability to make healthy choices with regard to non-communicable diseases and public sector has increased capacity to establish norms and regulations according to international standards and treaties
Output 4.1.6 - People (especially under 28 years old) have increased knowledge on health and improved healthy lifestyle behavior
Output 4.1.5 - The health system is strengthened to improve the quality, equity, and affordability of health services and medicines
Output 4.1.4 - Young women and men have knowledge and skills to enjoy well-being and apply democratic values, including gender equality, tolerance and non-violence
Output 4.1.3 - Education system is capable to provide safe environment, quality, inclusive learning and development for all

Output 4.1.2 - National and local authorities, and service providers are able to plan and provide social care services, implement preventive and productive measures and the population is aware about these services
Output 4.1.1 - Government has ability and instruments to take evidence-based policy decisions in line with the Social Protection Floor recommendation
Output 3.1.4 - Communities have new capabilities and services for sustainable and equitable access to natural resources, improved waste management, and promotion of green growth

Output 3.1.3 - National, local and community levels capacity are strengthened to implement i) climate change adaptation and mitigation measures, ii) sustainable energy solutions, and iii) sustainable NRM, disaster risk governance, and biodiversity conservation initiatives
Output 3.1.2 - Institutional capacities are strengthened for planning, resource mobilisation, monitoring, reporting and verification of climate change mitigation and adaptation, and DRM
Output 3.1.1 - Elements of national DRM/CC/IHR/Environmental policies, strategies and legal frameworks are strengthened to be risk-informed and gender responsive for building resilience
Output 2.1.4 - State institutions and communities, particularly youth and women, have new frameworks, capabilities, and programmes to prevent threats to sustainable peace

Output 2.1.3 - Justice system, law enforcement institutions and other relevant administrative bodies are able to uphold rule of law, promote and protect human rights, and provide access to justice services in line with human rights standards with particular attention to vulnerable groups

Output 2.1.2 - Women, youth, vulnerable groups, and civil society have new skills and greater access to resources to contribute, participate and be represented in decision making and governance at all levels and to demand their rights

Output 2.1.1 - Parliament, key ministries and agencies, LSGs have ability and instruments to effectively draft and implement evidence-based policies and legislation in compliance with international human rights and gender equality standards, and deliver effective, accountable and inclusive public services

Output 1.1.5 - Food insecure and vulnerable households, especially women & children, in the most vulnerable geographic areas of the KR have better access to basic services, productive assets and improved infrastructure

Output 1.1.4 - Capacities of MSMEs (Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises) and communities enhanced through access to innovative, energy-efficient and cost-effective green technologies and relevant business development services

Output 1.1.3 - Target groups have increased access to knowledge, skills, and opportunities to: diversify and improve their incomes, find decent and sustainable employment, and to take part in entrepreneurship and professional training for food security and nutrition
Output 1.1.2 - Improved public and private systems, tools and structures for enhanced socio-economic development

Output 1.1.1 - Institutions have improved capacity to formulate and implement coherent national, sectoral and cross-sectoral policies for sustainable and inclusive economic growth, decent work, improved livelihoods, agriculture, food security and nutrition
